rows.title: How a false X post about pausing tariffs led to multitrillion-dollar market swings
rows.standfirst: What began as a misquoted Fox News interview led to a flood of false and misleading posts on X. Before it was corrected, stock markets rallied then plummeted again.

rows.title: 'Every day, every single customer': Tariffs hit close to home inside Asian grocers
rows.standfirst: Asian grocery stores are a lifeline to the communities they serve. But store owners say the prospect of sweeping tariffs are threatening their ability to stock up on goods and keep prices affordable.

rows.title: Tariffs are fueling fears of a recession. What does it take to actually declare one?
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration's tariffs are fueling concerns about a potential recession, especially after the economy shrank in the first quarter of 2025. What is recession and who declares one?

rows.title: They had left their DEI roles. Trump still fired them
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration is firing hundreds and perhaps thousands of federal workers as part of a crackdown on diversity, equity and inclusion efforts. Many of the fired weren't in DEI jobs.

rows.title: Wall Street leaders warn of harsh economic consequences from Trump's tariffs
rows.standfirst: The business sector has tried to avoid criticizing Trump in public and welcomed his vows of lower taxes and deregulation, but the market sell-off appears to have loosened more tongues on Wall Street.

rows.title: Trump's tariffs complicate the Switch 2 launch, says Nintendo of America president
rows.standfirst: Some retailers appear to be cancelling preorders for the Nintendo Switch 2 ahead of the console's launch June 5. Nintendo of America President Doug Bowser spoke to us about how an ongoing trade war is impacting the Switch 2's release.

rows.title: Global markets plunge due to trade war. And, 2nd child dies in Texas from measles
rows.standfirst: Trump's trade war against most of the world has caused global markets to fall drastically. And, a second child in Texas has died from measles as the outbreak continues to spread.

rows.title: UAW President Shawn Fain explains why he supports Trump's tariffs
rows.standfirst: Shawn Fein supports auto industry tariffs but calls broad tariffs "reckless."

rows.title: Between tariffs and survival, American business owners are doing alarming math
rows.standfirst: Many U.S. shop owners feel like collateral damage in President Trump's trade war, on the hook to pay big new fees and long unable to manufacture in the U.S.

rows.title: Bracing for Trump's tariffs? Here are 3 money tips from a personal finance columnist
rows.standfirst: President Trump's new taxes on imported goods are creating a "scary ride" for the U.S. market, says personal finance columnist Michelle Singletary. She recommends keeping these three things in mind.

rows.title: Tariffied! We check in on businesses
rows.standfirst: Trump's wave of tariffs is here. Just about everyone in the world of business is still processing exactly what this means. It's a massive, widespread increase in taxes. Today on the show, we hear from business people we've had on the show who tell us what they're doing in response to the latest, and largest, wave of tariffs.

rows.title: U.S. stocks are volatile as selloffs sweep through global markets
rows.standfirst: Shares dropped around the world Monday as higher U.S. tariffs and a backlash from Beijing triggered massive sell-offs. Trump has defended the tariffs: "You have to take medicine to fix something."

rows.title: Jaguar and Land Rover maker pauses shipments to US as it develops post-tariff plans
rows.standfirst: Jaguar Land Rover Automotive said it was pausing U.S. shipments due to Trump's tariffs as it works on mid- to long-term plans to adapt to the changing trade landscape.

rows.title: How automakers are responding to the 25% car tariffs so far
rows.standfirst: It's only been a few days since President Trump's 25% tariffs on foreign cars took effect. But the import surcharge has led to some immediate changes, including layoffs and pauses in car shipments.

rows.title: Trump closes loophole used by American shoppers to buy Chinese goods tariff-free
rows.standfirst: The so-called de minimis exemption allowed Chinese and Hong Kong retailers to ship millions of packages worth $800 or less directly to U.S. consumers. That loophole will close May 2.

rows.title: Meta and the FTC face off in court over monopoly claims
rows.standfirst: Dozens of witnesses are set to take the stand in the trial, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg, who is scheduled to testify for seven hours. The outcome could reshape the future of Meta.

rows.title: Katy Perry, Gayle King and others reflect on their brief but historic trip to space
rows.standfirst: Monday's 11-minute flight featured the first all-female crew since 1963. Here's what else to know about it.

rows.title: How much is a weather forecast worth? (Update)
rows.standfirst: The federal government has been tracking the weather for more than 150 years. But the rise of the Internet and big tech have made weather forecasting a more crowded space. Today on the show, the value of an accurate forecast and how the Trump administration's early moves are clouding the government's future forecasting. This piece originally aired in November 2024.

rows.title: Trump mulls semiconductor levies after lifting reciprocal tariffs on electronics
rows.standfirst: Trump targets Chinese technology with 20% fentanyl tariff and eyes semiconductors in a "National Security Tariff Investigation" over coming months.

rows.title: The biggest trial in Meta's history starts Monday. Here's what to know
rows.standfirst: The government plans to call Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg to the witness stand. The trial is expected to run nearly two months in a federal courtroom in Washington.

rows.title: A retrial of Sarah Palin's case against 'New York Times' begins Monday
rows.standfirst: Former Alaska Gov. Sarah Palin has the rare opportunity to retry her defamation case against The New York Times even though she lost it — twice in a 24-hour-period — in early 2022.

rows.title: Smartphones and computers are now spared from Trump's reciprocal tariffs
rows.standfirst: The exemption comes amid worries of how President Trump's steep new tariffs will affect American tech companies that rely on supply chains in China, like Apple.

rows.title: China put steep tariffs on U.S. exports. Farmers are worried
rows.standfirst: The first Trump administration spent $28 billion bailing out farmers during a trade war with China. The White House has said it's starting to look at how to help this time around.

rows.title: Trade war dispatch from Canada
rows.standfirst: How do you run a business when a trade war is brewing? As President Trump's tariffs kick in - or are paused or are restarted - businesses around the world are trying to navigate the uncertainty.

rows.title: Are Trump's tariffs a bargaining chip for a new global economic order?
rows.standfirst: It's not just tariffs. The White House is rethinking the central role of the dollar in the global economy.

rows.title: How to get what you want without using cash (you read that right)
rows.standfirst: For many of us, when we see something we want, we pull out our cards and swipe for it. Instead, try this resourceful approach.

rows.title: Will tariffs drive more people to shop secondhand? It's a mixed bag, experts say
rows.standfirst: This moment of economic uncertainty could drive more Americans to buy used. But experts say secondhand stores won't be immune from tariffs either.

rows.title: Beijing slaps 125% tariffs on U.S. goods in latest U.S.-China trade escalation
rows.standfirst: China signals the latest tariff hike will be its last round of tit-for-tat measures, prompting sharp falls in European shares, as Asian stocks end the day mixed.

rows.title: IRS information sharing, bonds bust, and a chorebot future
rows.standfirst: Today on the show, we discuss why the IRS is sharing some taxpayer information, why bonds and stocks both fell, and how robots will replace you,or at least most of your chore wheel, in the near future.

rows.title: Lipstick, sunscreen, & this podcast are recession indicators
rows.standfirst: Global markets got a case of the jitters this week in the wake of President Trump's global tariff policy. Everyone from hedge fund managers to online content creators have been starting to question the stability of America's economic trajectory. We're now seeing increased fear that a recession is just around the corner.

rows.title: The Brave Souls take on icy waters in this College Podcast Challenge entry
rows.standfirst: A group called the "Brave Souls" plunge into icy river waters each week -- a podcast about them is a finalist in NPR's College Podcast Challenge.

rows.title: The Justice Department and Google battle over how to fix a search engine monopoly
rows.standfirst: After a federal judge ruled that Google had a monopoly on the search market, the tech giant and the government are in court to debate penalties. One possible result: forcing Google to spin off Chrome.

rows.title: DHL will stop shipping packages over $800 to U.S. customers due to new customs rules
rows.standfirst: The shipping company's temporary new policy comes as President Trump continues to upend U.S. global trade policy.

rows.title: China warns of 'countermeasures' against any deals that harm its interests
rows.standfirst: The comments come after reports that Trump is hoping to use tariff negotiations with other countries to isolate China.

rows.title: Sell USA? Why Trump's tariffs may be sparking a historic storm on Wall Street
rows.standfirst: When Trump announced sweeping tariffs this month, he called it "Liberation Day." But there are fears that it may well have been the day foreign investors started to lose faith in the United States.

rows.title: A trap-loving DJ takes on economics
rows.standfirst: It's time for The Indicator Quiz! We test you, dear listener, on your knowledge of topics that we've covered on The Indicator.

rows.title: The Justice Department is about to make its case for a Google breakup. Here's what to know
rows.standfirst: Google and the Justice Department will face off in the final stage of a landmark antitrust case that could force the company to spin off its Chrome browser business.

rows.title: Cuts to federal grants affecting even non-profits that don't get them
rows.standfirst: Big cuts to federal grants are now affecting non-profits that don't get federal support because private foundations are being swamped with requests to fill funding gaps.

rows.title: Amazon and Meta are among the corporate sponsors of the White House Easter Egg Roll
rows.standfirst: Corporate sponsors for the usually apolitical event held on the White House South Lawn include tech giants Meta, YouTube and Amazon.

rows.title: How much for that egg
rows.standfirst: Recently, one of our NPR colleagues wrote a message to all of NPR saying he had extra eggs to sell for cheap, but needed a fair way to distribute them during a shortage. What is Planet Money here for if not to get OVERLY involved in this kind of situation?

rows.title: Chinese manufacturers on TikTok claim they make the world's luxury goods. Is that true?
rows.standfirst: Amid tariff confusion, online vendors are looking to recruit new customers.

rows.title: Tariffs threaten to push auto insurance rates even higher
rows.standfirst: Between the slate of tariffs currently in effect and proposed tariffs on car parts, the cost of car ownership is rising. And that's true even if you're not in the market for a vehicle.

rows.title: Judge blocks mass layoffs at CFPB in the latest twist over the fate of the agency
rows.standfirst: In declarations to federal court, CFPB employees describe a hasty process to eliminate most of the agency's staff. "[A]ll that matters is the numbers," one employee said they were told by leaders.

rows.title: Raising kids is costly; Tariffs will make it even more expensive
rows.standfirst: When it comes to the cost of raising a child from infancy to the age of 17 in the United States – it's hard to settle on a precise figure.

rows.title: How tariffs could impact the availability of baby products
rows.standfirst: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Steven Dunn founder and CEO of Munchkin a U.S.-based company selling lifestyle products for mothers, babies and children. Dunn has written an open letter to President Trump and Congress about how tariffs could harm his business and American families.

rows.title: Ford Motor CEO 'welcomes' Trump's move to ease tariffs on automakers
rows.standfirst: President Trump is easing some of his tariffs on the U.S. auto industry. But what will the overall impact of these economic policies mean for the nation's biggest carmakers? Ford Motor CEO weighs in.

rows.title: Tariffs making you anxious about money? Here's some advice from a financial expert
rows.standfirst: With stock market volatility and fears of price increases driven by the new tariffs, you may be worried about your finances. A certified financial planner explains how to navigate these tricky times.

rows.title: In court, CEO Sundar Pichai defends Google against the DOJ's 'extraordinary' proposals
rows.standfirst: Sundar Pichai testified in the remedies trial that will determine the penalties Google will face for monopolizing the search engine market.

rows.title: Private eye accused of hacking American climate activists loses U.K. extradition fight
rows.standfirst: The Justice Department has charged Amit Forlit with conspiracy to commit computer hacking, among other crimes.

rows.title: The U.S. economy shrinks as Trump's tariffs spark recession fears
rows.standfirst: Trump promised a new "golden age" for the U.S. But his first 100 days in office have left the economy looking tarnished, with data showing the economy contracted in the first three months of the year.

rows.title: How stable is Stablecoin?
rows.standfirst: Stablecoins are the latest digital asset to grab headlines. Congress is considering legislation around the cryptocurrency, and a Trump family-affiliated company is preparing to launch its own Stablecoin. But does this digital currency live up to its own name?

rows.title: Planet Money complains. To learn.
rows.standfirst: On today's show: we're ... venting.

rows.title: Why Google's search engine trial is about AI
rows.standfirst: What started off as an antitrust trial about Google's dominance in the search engine market has led to a penalties phase that is focused on its role in artificial intelligence.

rows.title: Corporation for Public Broadcasting sues Trump after he tries to fire board members
rows.standfirst: Hours after President Trump tried to remove three board members, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting responds with a lawsuit arguing he does not have that authority.

rows.title: Trump called Bezos after a report that Amazon would post products' import charges
rows.standfirst: After a news report earlier Tuesday, Amazon spokesperson Tim Doyle said a team only considered listing import charges on items in its ultra-low-cost store. "This was never approved and is not going to happen."

rows.title: New lawsuit argues Trump and DOGE's government overhaul is unconstitutional
rows.standfirst: A coalition of unions, nonprofits and local governments has sued President Trump, Elon Musk and the heads of nearly two dozen agencies in an effort to block mass layoffs in the federal government.

rows.title: A weird partisan pattern of trust in the Fed
rows.standfirst: A new study shows how partisan politics has long influenced whether Americans trust the Fed. And how, with Trump's second term, an old pattern may have changed.

rows.title: More give Trump an F than any other grade for first 100 days, poll finds
rows.standfirst: Nearly half of Americans give President Trump a failing grade for his presidency so far, with near record low approval ratings at this point in the job, as he hits the milestone 100 days in office.

rows.title: Amazon launches its first internet satellites to compete against SpaceX's Starlinks
rows.standfirst: Stargazers oppose the fast-growing constellations of low-orbiting satellites, arguing they spoil observations. Others fear more satellite collisions.

rows.title: Trump is giving automakers a break on tariffs
rows.standfirst: President Trump signed executive actions as the White House marks his 100 days in office. It's the latest shift in Trump's on-again, off-again approach to tariffs.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
